result.summary: This PR implements BIP-119 OP_CHECKTEMPLATEVERIFY, activating it only on regtest via a new versionbits deployment, with no policy or consensus change on mainnet/testnet. It adds the CTV script opcode, hash computation, standardness rule for bare CTV outputs, deployment/softfork RPC reporting, and extensive unit, script, and functional test coverage. The stated purpose is to let CTV-based use cases be built and tested without altering live network rules, and to allow composition with other proposed opcodes (CSFS, CAT) in a future bundled deployment.
result.problem: CTV has been proposed for years as a minimal covenant primitive enabling vaults, congestion trees, and non-custodial payout batching, but there is no regtest-only implementation in Core for developers to test against, and no rough consensus among Bitcoin users or developers on whether to activate it at all.

categories.name: validation
categories.evidence: Adds a new versionbits deployment (DEPLOYMENT_CTV), a new SCRIPT_VERIFY_CHECKTEMPLATEVERIFY flag enforced in GetBlockScriptFlags and PolicyScriptChecks, and new consensus-affecting opcode semantics in interpreter.cpp; this is a proposed soft fork.
categories.rationale: Per the validation category's own rule, a proposed soft fork like this is P1 because reaching a decision on it (and having correct code if activated) matters regardless of whether the fork itself is wanted. The PR has been open 561 days with unresolved Concept NACKs (darosior, BitcoinErrorLog) disputing whether Core should carry consensus-changing code without community consensus, which is exactly the kind of blocking decision the P1 band is meant to flag.

categories.name: mempool
categories.evidence: Adds a standardness rule in policy.cpp/h for bare CTV outputs (scriptSig must be empty) and a new STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS bit for discouraging CTV pre-activation.
categories.rationale: The description states 'There is no effective policy change, since the SCRIPT_VERIFY_* flags... result in the same NOP-like behavior' outside regtest, so mainnet mempool policy is unaffected today. The policy hook only matters if/when CTV activates elsewhere, making this a real but currently dormant policy addition.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: Adds CTV softfork reporting to getdeploymentinfo (rpc/blockchain.cpp) and decodescript handling for the new TxoutType (rpc/rawtransaction.cpp).
categories.rationale: These are mechanical additions needed so existing RPCs stay consistent with the new opcode and deployment, gated to regtest only; no external consumer has asked for this RPC surface, per category guidance that 'new methods without an external consumer asking rank low.'

categories.name: tests
categories.evidence: The bulk of new tests (feature_checktemplateverify.py, ctvhash.json, ctvhash_tests.cpp, tx_valid/tx_invalid additions) pin CTV's own consensus behavior rather than adding general test-framework capability.
categories.rationale: Per the tests category definition, 'a test that pins the behavior of one area... belongs to that area, not here'; the framework touches (script.py opcode rename, a CTV-specific hashing helper in messages.py) are mechanical follow-ons of the CTV feature, not new general framework capability.

categories.name: wallet
categories.evidence: scriptpubkeyman.cpp adds a switch case returning IsMineResult::NO for the new TxoutType, required only to keep the exhaustive switch compiling.
categories.rationale: This is exactly the kind of mechanical call-site update the rules exclude from membership: it follows automatically from adding a new TxoutType enum value elsewhere, with no wallet-specific design or behavior change.

categories.name: kernel
categories.evidence: kernel/chainparams.cpp is touched only to add regtest consensus deployment parameters for CTV, not to change the libbitcoinkernel API or its boundary.
categories.rationale: The change does not touch the kernel C/C++ API, notifications, or the node/library boundary; it is a consensus-parameter addition that happens to live in a file under src/kernel.

uncertainties: Whether the CTV opcode implementation itself has unresolved bugs is not something this pass verified; the code has received several rounds of contributor code review (JeremyRubin, average-gary) but no maintainer sign-off.

Whether the block-sigop/weight overflow concern ariard raised is a real vulnerability requiring a fix in this PR versus being orthogonal to CTV is disputed between ariard and the author and not resolved.

The true current staleness is uncertain: signals show author_silent_days=442 while last_author_activity is 2025-07-01, suggesting the 'now' reference date used for signals is well over a year after that push; treated Stale based on the provided signal.
result.card: This PR implements BIP-119 OP_CHECKTEMPLATEVERIFY, but activates it only on regtest via a new versionbits deployment, so it has no effect on mainnet or testnet policy or consensus today. It is a proposed soft fork intended to let developers build and test covenant-style contracts (vaults, congestion trees, non-custodial mining payout batching) without live network risk, and to allow future bundling with other proposed opcodes like CSFS or CAT. The strongest evidence of its stakes is the unresolved Concept NACKs from darosior and BitcoinErrorLog, both arguing there is no rough community consensus to justify Bitcoin Core carrying this consensus-change code, met by several Concept ACKs citing concrete use cases; the author has not directly responded to either NACK. The PR needs a rebase and the author has been silent for well over a year, so review right now risks being invalidated by a future rebase. Within validation this is P1 because a decision on proposed soft forks is itself category-critical; in mempool and rpc its current impact is minor since the feature is dormant outside regtest.
